diagnosis.root_cause: The router has no recorded monitoring heartbeat or check-in, so it is unreachable to the monitoring system or has never been enrolled correctly. Customer service is nevertheless active, with a serving ONU, established RADIUS session, assigned IP, and normal traffic.
evidence: The scheduled scan specifically targets the router, whose last_checkin is null and heartbeat_status is never.
A heartbeat value of never means there has never been a monitoring record; this indicates a monitoring or management reachability problem rather than a recent service outage.
The ONU is online and responding, with RX power of -21.9 dBm and TX power of 2.34 dBm, both normal.

The customer's optical telemetry is stable over seven days: RX variation is within the healthy noise range, TX variation is within the healthy noise range, distance remains constant at 87, and TX bias current remains healthy without an ageing trend.
The OLT is reachable and healthy: all six PONs passed, CPU is 22%, memory is 17%, and temperature is 40C.
The customer has normal authentication behavior with 3 sessions in 24 hours, 17 in seven days, and an average session duration of about 11.4 hours.
RADIUS data, line ID, assigned IP, CRM records, and VLAN 1124 are consistent.
Traffic is present and stable, confirming that the subscriber is currently being served.
There is no evidence for fibre degradation, ONU offline status, PON or OLT failure, authentication flapping, VLAN 46 provisioning, duplicate ONU assignment, or PON congestion.

remediation.action: Verify management-plane reachability to router TK_Skopje15-Madzari01, including routing, firewall rules, SNMP/API credentials, monitoring-agent configuration, and device enrollment. Restore or configure the heartbeat/check-in mechanism and rerun the router probe. Do not dispatch for fibre, ONU, OLT, VLAN, or authentication work unless the router remains unreachable after management checks.

ground_truth.root_cause: The router has no check-in record of any kind, which means it was never enrolled in heartbeat monitoring rather than that it stopped responding. Its customers are authenticated, holding long sessions and passing normal traffic.
expected_reasoning: The router's heartbeat status is 'never' with a null last_checkin
That is different from a heartbeat that went stale, which would carry a timestamp and an elapsed time
No record at all indicates the router was never enrolled in the check-in mechanism
The ONU behind it is online with RX -21.9 and TX 2.3, both normal
The live probe confirms the ONU and its peers are all responding normally
Sessions are active with a 683 minute mean, close to the 11.9 hour network norm
Daily traffic is steady across all seven days with no interruption
Customers on this router are being served, so there is no outage
The finding is a monitoring gap, not a network fault

expected_escalation.review_reason: Router is not enrolled in heartbeat monitoring and should be added

distractors: A null heartbeat looks worse than a stale one and invites a Disaster conclusion
A scheduled scan targeting the router frames it as the suspect
The correct answer is that nothing is wrong with the network
